question.:question/worked-solution:
This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse tangent,

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have $144{x}^{2}=(12x)^{2}.$

So. let's substitute $u=12x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=12\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{12}\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{24}{1+144{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =24\int \frac{1}{1+(12x)^{2}}\text{d}x \\  & =24\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\cdot (\frac{1}{12}\text{d}u) \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(12x)+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{144+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{144\cdot (1+{x}^{2}/144)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{144}\int \frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}/144}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{144}\int \frac{1}{1+(x/12)^{2}}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse tangent

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have ${(\frac{x}{12})}^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{x}{12}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{12}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=12\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{144+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{144}\int \frac{1}{1+(x/12)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{144}\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\cdot (12\,\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}\int \frac{\text{d}u}{1+{u}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{1}{12}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{12})+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
